messages:
support-alex: Heads-up: customer @jessica (org: org_12345 / acme-co) reported their org showed 0 credits for ~30m right before monthly refill. They were getting 429s on generation. Happened while we were doing a planned regional failover. Raising here so eng/sre/infra can triage.

customer-jessica: Repro notes from their side — timeline: 2026-03-01 00:09 local. Calls to our API returned 429s with X-RateLimit: 0. Example call they ran: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/orgs/org_12345/credits"
```
Response body they saw: 
```json
{"available":0,"next_refill":"2026-03-01T00:00:00-03:00"}
```
They say the UI showed 0 for ~20-30 minutes and then suddenly refilled. They were on eu-west region and we were failing over to eu-west-2 at the time.

dylan-eng: Thanks. Do we have the customer request_id / x-request-id from those 429s? Also paste the 429 response headers if available. Any deploys/ops windows?

support-alex: Request id from customer: req_0a1b2c3d4e. 429 response headers (copied by customer): 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 00:12:03 GMT
X-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d4e
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 184
```

infra-bot: Ops note: automated region failover kicked at 2026-03-01T00:10:17Z due to scheduled maintenance in sa-east. Control plane initiated DB primary election (billing-primary promoted in eu-west-2). Some write-forwarding to billing DB queued during promotion window. Cache invalidation job started but had backlog.

priya-sre: Looking at logs — we see a read-after-write inconsistency window. Steps: 
1) At 00:10:20Z a refill job attempted to write +12000 tokens for org_12345 into billing-primary but the write was enqueued until 00:28:05Z because the writer pod was being drained and mounting a new replica set.
2) Meanwhile the CDN + cache layer served a cached value of 0 from a sticky cache node (eu-west-1) due to sentinel replication lag. Redis GET for key credits:org_12345 at 00:12:00Z returned 0; after writer backfill at 00:28:06Z GET returned 12000.

priya-sre: Relevant debug snippets we pulled: 
```
# internal debug endpoint (prod-only)
GET /internal/debug/redis/credits?org=org_12345
=> {"node":"eu-west-1-sticky-3","value":0,"ttl":120}

# billing write log
[2026-03-01T00:28:05Z] billing-writer: backfilling refill for org_12345 amount=12000 job_id=jb_42f
```

billing-ops: Clarifying refill semantics: monthly refill runs at the tenant billing timezone midnight (customer's timezone) which schedules a refill job. The refill job writes to the canonical billing DB (UTC timestamps). If the DB primary is unavailable or being promoted during that window, the write can be delayed. Our API reads primarily from cache for performance; when cache holds stale zero during a write delay, customers can see 0 until the write+cache invalidation complete.

dylan-eng: That matches what we see. Root cause appears to be the intersection of (A) a scheduled region failover that caused a billing writer promotion/drain, and (B) a sticky cache node that served stale values for longer than our expected replication window. Two problems: write was delayed ~18m, and cache entry didn't expire/replicate as expected.

support-alex: Customer asked why the UI didn't fall back to a conservative 'safety' read from payments DB or show a queued refill indicator. Any short-term workaround we can offer them?

priya-sre: Short-term: we can run an immediate backfill for this tenant (we already did the write) and invalidate caches for org_12345; telling the customer to try POST /v1/admin/usage/refresh (internal support-only endpoint) will force re-read from billing DB and invalidate cache. Example: 
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-support" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/orgs/org_12345/_refresh_credits"
```
This should show correct credits immediately. We executed the backfill at 00:28 and cache invalidation at 00:28:10, after which the customer saw credits return.

billing-ops: We notified the customer and documented that their refill timestamp remains their timezone midnight; the visible delay was operational. They were ok with the explanation but want assurance this won't recur.

dylan-eng: Proposed next steps (action items): 
- Add a small write-forwarding retry queue so refill jobs are retried immediately to any available writer replica (owner: billing team)
- Harden cache replication policy and reduce sticky-node TTLs during failovers (owner: infra/sre)
- Add an alert when refill job write latency > 5s (owner: ops monitoring)
- Add a user-facing UI hint that refill may be delayed during maintenance windows (owner: product)

priya-sre: Also adding a short-term guard: if cache returns 0 and the refill window is within +/- 5 minutes, attempt a direct DB read before serving 0. That avoids visible zero for most cases.

support-alex: Customer confirm: they got credits back at ~00:28 local and were able to continue. They asked for the incident reference; billing-ops will create an incident report for outreach.

billing-ops: Incident created: INC-2026-0301-034. We will follow up with a short postmortem and the timeline + mitigations.

customer-jessica: Thanks for the quick follow-up and the explanation, appreciate the transparency :thumbsup:

dylan-eng: Marking this resolved for now. If anyone sees more tenants with similar symptoms during the maintenance window, please @priya-sre and escalate. :white_check_mark:
